title: The Brave Diver's Discovery
summary: A girl training in free-diving with her uncle notices an unusual rock formation on a reef, and together they work with a marine scientist to understand what she found.
poll: Ordinary people, not just scientists, can make important discoveries.

versions.title: The Brave Diver's Discovery
versions.text:
Reem dives with her uncle. His name is Uncle Faisal. They dive by the reef. They dive each week. Reem learns to hold her breath. She stays calm in the sea.

One day, Reem sees a strange thing. She sees straight lines on the reef. The lines look like a ridge. It does not look like other coral.

Reem swims up. She takes a breath. She tells her uncle what she saw. He says, "Do not touch it. Just look at it."

They dive down again. They look at the ridge and are very careful. They do not touch it. Uncle Faisal takes a photo.

That night, he sends the photo to Dr. Huda. She studies the sea. Dr. Huda says the ridge may be rare. She wants to see it, too.

Dr. Huda comes to the reef. She dives with Reem and her uncle. She looks at the ridge. She says it is a rare find.

Dr. Huda thanks Reem. Reem has sharp eyes. Reem feels proud. She wants to study the sea one day, too.

versions.title: The Brave Diver's Discovery
versions.text:
Reem has spent the past year training to be a free-diver with her uncle, Faisal. Free-diving means swimming deep underwater without a tank of air, using just one breath. Every week, near the reef by their town, Reem practices holding her breath and staying calm as she swims down.

One Friday morning, during a practice dive, Reem notices something unusual near the edge of the reef. She sees rows of straight lines forming a ridge. The pattern does not match the coral growing around it.

She swims up for air and tells her uncle what she found. He is curious too, but he reminds her of an important rule: "Never touch anything on the reef. We will only examine it with our eyes."

Together, they dive back down and study the ridge without disturbing it. Uncle Faisal takes several photographs with his camera so they can study the formation more closely later.

That evening, Uncle Faisal sends the photographs to Dr. Huda, a marine scientist who studies the reefs of the Red Sea. After looking at the photos, Dr. Huda thinks the ridge may be an unusual formation. She plans a visit to see it herself.

A few days later, Dr. Huda arrives with a small survey team. She dives with Reem and Uncle Faisal to look closely at the ridge. After a careful look, she confirms it is a rare and valuable find.

Dr. Huda praises Reem for her sharp eyes and for being careful not to disturb the reef. Reem feels proud of her part in the find. From then on, she trains harder than ever, dreaming of becoming a marine scientist herself one day.

versions.title: The Brave Diver's Discovery
versions.text:
Reem has spent the past year training to become a free-diver with her uncle, Faisal, who has taught her everything she knows about the sport. Free-diving means swimming deep underwater without a tank of compressed air, relying entirely on a single held breath instead. Every week, near the reef by their coastal town, Reem practices holding her breath and staying calm while she glides downward through the clear water.

One Friday morning, during a routine practice dive, Reem notices something unusual near the edge of the reef. She sees rows of straight lines forming a distinct ridge, and its pattern does not match the coral growing naturally all around it.

She swims up for air and tells her uncle what she found. He is curious as well, but he reminds her of an important rule that experienced divers always follow: "Never touch anything on the reef. We will only examine it carefully with our eyes, nothing more than that."

Together, they dive back down and study the ridge without disturbing it in any way. Uncle Faisal takes several photographs with his underwater camera so that they can study the strange formation more closely that night.

That evening, Uncle Faisal sends the photographs to Dr. Huda, a marine scientist who has devoted many years to studying the coral reef ecosystem of the Red Sea. After examining the photographs closely, Dr. Huda suspects the ridge may actually be a fossil, the preserved remains of an ancient coral colony hidden beneath the newer, living coral. She plans a visit to identify it with certainty.

A few days later, Dr. Huda arrives with a small survey team of her colleagues. She dives with Reem and Uncle Faisal to inspect the ridge up close. After studying samples and comparing the pattern to known fossil records from similar expeditions elsewhere, the team confirms it is indeed a rare fossilized coral colony, one worth preserving and protecting from any future damage.

Dr. Huda praises Reem for her sharp observation skills and for being careful not to disturb the fragile fossil while investigating it. Reem feels genuinely proud of her part in the discovery, and Dr. Huda invites her to join future surveys of the ecosystem as a young reef observer. From then on, Reem trains harder than ever, dreaming of becoming a marine scientist herself one day.

versions.title: The Brave Diver's Discovery
versions.text:
Reem has spent the past year training to become a proficient free-diver under the patient instruction of her uncle, Faisal, who has gradually taught her everything he knows about the demanding sport. Free-diving requires swimming to considerable depths without any tank of compressed air, relying entirely on a single held breath instead of mechanical breathing equipment. Every week, near the reef beside their coastal town, Reem practices holding her breath and remaining perfectly calm while gliding downward through the clear, sunlit water.

One Friday morning, during an otherwise ordinary practice dive, Reem notices something distinctly unusual near the outer edge of the reef. She observes rows of unnaturally straight lines forming a prominent ridge, and its geometric pattern fails to match the irregular coral formations growing naturally all around it.

She swims upward for air and immediately tells her uncle what she has discovered. He is equally curious, but he reminds her of an important rule that experienced divers always follow without exception: "Never touch anything on the reef. We will only examine it carefully with our eyes, nothing more than that."

Together, they dive back down and study the ridge thoroughly without disturbing it in any way whatsoever. Uncle Faisal captures several photographs with his underwater camera so that they can examine the peculiar formation more closely once they return home that night.

That evening, Uncle Faisal forwards the photographs to Dr. Huda, a marine scientist who has devoted many years to studying the coral reef ecosystem of the Red Sea in considerable detail. After examining the photographs with great interest, Dr. Huda suspects the ridge may actually be a fossil, the preserved remains of an ancient coral colony hidden beneath newer, living coral growth. She immediately arranges a visit to identify it with scientific certainty.

A few days later, Dr. Huda arrives accompanied by a small survey team composed of her professional colleagues. She dives alongside Reem and Uncle Faisal to inspect the ridge at close range. After studying collected samples and comparing the distinctive pattern to known fossil records from similar expeditions conducted elsewhere, the team confirms that it is indeed a rare fossilized coral colony, one undeniably worth preserving and protecting from any future damage.

Dr. Huda warmly praises Reem for her remarkably sharp observation skills and for being careful not to disturb the fragile fossil while investigating it so closely. Reem feels genuinely proud of her significant part in the discovery, and Dr. Huda graciously invites her to join future surveys of the ecosystem as a young reef observer. From that moment onward, Reem trains even harder than she ever had before, dreaming of eventually becoming a marine scientist herself, just like the remarkable woman who taught her so much.

keyWords.definition: to go underwater, usually head first
keyWords.example: The dolphin dove deep to find fish.

keyWords.definition: a line of rock or coral near the surface of the sea
keyWords.example: Colorful fish swam around the busy reef.

keyWords.definition: the air that goes into and out of your lungs
keyWords.example: She took a deep breath before jumping into the pool.

keyWords.definition: a long, raised line or strip on a surface
keyWords.example: The hiker walked along a rocky ridge on the mountain.

keyWords.definition: paying close attention so you do not make a mistake or cause harm
keyWords.example: Be careful when you carry the glass cups.

questions.stem: What is this article mostly about?
options: A girl who learns to ride a boat
A girl who finds something strange on a reef and tells a scientist
A scientist who builds a new reef
A girl who is afraid of going into deep, dark ocean water at all
questions.why: The article tells how Reem notices a strange ridge while diving and helps Dr. Huda learn about it.

wrong.A: The article is not about riding boats.
wrong.C: Dr. Huda studies the ridge; she does not build a reef.
wrong.D: Reem is not afraid of the water. She trains to dive in it.

questions.stem: How does Reem dive?
options: With a big tank of air
In a boat with a net
Without any tank, holding her breath
With large rubber fins attached to her feet
questions.why: The article says Reem is a free-diver, which means she does not use a tank. She holds her breath instead.

wrong.A: A free-diver does not use a tank.
wrong.B: Reem dives in the water, not in a boat.
wrong.D: The article never mentions wings.

questions.stem: What did Reem see on the reef?
options: Rows of straight lines like a ridge
A sunken boat
A group of sharks
A large pile of dark, leaking engine oil on the sand
questions.why: In the story, Reem sees straight lines on the reef.

wrong.B: The article does not mention a sunken boat.
wrong.C: The article does not mention sharks.
wrong.D: The article does not mention oil.

questions.stem: Why does Uncle Faisal tell Reem only to look, not to touch?
options: He is tired and wants to go home
They might get in trouble with the mayor
Touching is strictly against all of the posted rules of the swimming pool
He wants to keep the strange thing safe until they know what it is
questions.why: Since they do not yet know what the ridge is, not touching it keeps it safe from harm.

wrong.A: The article does not say he is tired.
wrong.B: The article does not mention a mayor.
wrong.C: This is a reef, not a pool.

questions.stem: Why does Dr. Huda want to see the ridge for herself?
options: She wants to swim for fun in the cool water
She thinks it might be a rare and important find
She needs new photos for her phone and her friends
She wants to meet Uncle Faisal's friends at the reef
questions.why: Dr. Huda thinks the ridge may be rare, so she travels to see it herself and check.

wrong.A: She comes to study the ridge, not to swim for fun.
wrong.C: Uncle Faisal already sent her a photo.
wrong.D: The article does not mention meeting friends.

questions.stem: In the article, a ridge is —
options: a kind of fish that lives in a lake
a type of boat used by fishermen
a raised line or row, like a small hill
a deep hole in the sand of the desert
questions.why: The article describes the ridge as rows of straight lines, like a raised line on the reef.

wrong.A: A ridge is not a fish.
wrong.B: A ridge is not a boat.
wrong.D: A ridge rises up; it is not a hole.

questions.stem: Why does the author begin the article by describing Reem's training with Uncle Faisal?
options: To show that Reem is a careful, well-trained diver before she makes her discovery
To explain how to build a boat for fishing in the sea and to sail it on the waves
To teach readers about fish and sea animals that live on the reef and in the deep
To show that diving is not allowed in the Red Sea and that it is a crime for children
questions.why: Knowing Reem trains carefully helps readers understand how she was prepared to notice the ridge safely.

wrong.B: The article does not explain how to build a boat.
wrong.C: The article is not a lesson about fish.
wrong.D: The article shows Reem diving often, so diving is clearly allowed.

questions.stem: Which happens first in the story?
options: Dr. Huda visits the reef
Reem notices the ridge while diving
Uncle Faisal sends photos to Dr. Huda
Dr. Huda thanks Reem for her sharp eyes
questions.why: Reem must notice the ridge before anyone can tell Dr. Huda or thank Reem for finding it.

wrong.C: The photos are sent after Reem finds the ridge.
wrong.D: Dr. Huda thanks Reem near the end of the story.

LOW.prompt: Would you want to train as a free-diver like Reem? Explain why or why not, using at least two facts from the article.
checklist: I clearly said what I think.
I used at least two facts from the article.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: I would want to train as a free-diver like Reem. I would like to learn how to hold my breath and stay calm underwater without a heavy tank. I also like that Reem's careful diving helped her notice the strange ridge on the reef. Because she was patient and careful, she helped a real scientist learn something new.

keyWords.definition: the way something is shaped or arranged
keyWords.example: The birds flew in a V-shaped formation.

keyWords.definition: a design that repeats, or a way something regularly happens
keyWords.example: The rug had a pattern of blue and white squares.

keyWords.definition: to look at something closely and carefully
keyWords.example: The doctor examined the boy's arm after the fall.

keyWords.definition: having to do with the sea or ocean
keyWords.example: A marine biologist studies animals that live in the sea.

keyWords.definition: a careful study of an area made to gather information
keyWords.example: The team did a survey of the old forest before building the trail.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the article?
options: A young free-diver notices an unusual formation on a reef and helps a marine scientist examine it.
Reem is afraid of deep water and she never goes to the beach or the sea with her family.
A diver loses her camera in the sea and spends a whole week looking for it with her friends.
Dr. Huda spends her time teaching free-diving lessons to young students every week.
questions.why: The article follows Reem's discovery of the unusual ridge and how it leads to Dr. Huda examining it.

wrong.B: Reem trains to dive bravely; she is not shown as afraid.
wrong.C: The camera is used to take photos, not lost.
wrong.D: Dr. Huda is a marine scientist, not a diving teacher.

questions.stem: What is Reem training to become?
options: A boat captain
A lifeguard
A free-diver
A fisherman
questions.why: The article states that Reem is training to be a free-diver with her uncle.

wrong.A: There is no mention of boat captains.
wrong.B: The article never calls Reem a lifeguard.
wrong.D: The article does not describe her as a fisherman.

questions.stem: What was unusual about the pattern Reem noticed?
options: It looked exactly the same as all the ordinary coral growing around it
It glowed in the dark
It moved with the current
It did not match the coral growing around it
questions.why: The article says the pattern of straight lines did not match the coral growing around it.

wrong.A: The article says the opposite: it did not match the coral.
wrong.B: The article never mentions glowing.
wrong.C: The article never mentions movement.

questions.stem: In the article, to examine something means to —
options: touch it quickly
look at it closely and carefully
throw it away
carefully take it home in a small plastic bag
questions.why: Uncle Faisal tells Reem they will only examine the ridge with their eyes, meaning look closely without touching.

wrong.A: The rule is not to touch it at all.
wrong.C: They do not throw the ridge away.
wrong.D: A reef ridge cannot be taken home.

questions.stem: Why does Uncle Faisal remind Reem of the rule about not touching the reef?
options: Touching could damage something they do not understand yet
He does not trust Reem
It is strictly against the law for anyone to swim near that part of the reef
The reef is too far away
questions.why: Since the formation is unidentified, touching it risks damaging something that may turn out to be important.

wrong.B: The article shows he trusts and praises Reem.
wrong.C: The article never mentions this being illegal.
wrong.D: They swim there often, so it is clearly not too far.

questions.stem: Why does Dr. Huda decide to visit the reef herself instead of just looking at photographs?
options: She wants a vacation at the sea and thinks the trip will be a fun holiday
She does not trust Uncle Faisal's camera and thinks the photographs are fake
She lives near the reef and can walk there in a few minutes each day
The formation seems unusual enough that she needs to examine it directly
questions.why: Dr. Huda suspects the formation is unusual, so she plans a visit to investigate it more closely herself.

wrong.A: She comes to study the reef, not to relax.
wrong.B: The article gives no reason to doubt the camera.
wrong.C: The article does not say where Dr. Huda lives.

questions.stem: What is the result of the team's close examination of the ridge?
options: They decide it is ordinary coral after all
They decide to remove it from the reef and sell it
They confirm it is a rare and valuable formation
They lose interest in it and go home
questions.why: After studying the ridge carefully, the team confirms that it truly is a rare and valuable find.

wrong.A: The team confirms it is unusual, not ordinary.
wrong.B: The article never mentions removing it.
wrong.D: The team becomes more interested, not less.

questions.stem: How does the author organize the article?
options: By comparing two different reefs near the coast and what lives on each one
By following events in order, from training, to discovery, to the scientist's visit
By explaining the steps to repair a boat on the shore, from the first nail to the last
By listing facts about every sea animal in the ocean, from the smallest to the biggest
questions.why: The article moves in order: Reem's training, her discovery, telling her uncle, and Dr. Huda's visit and confirmation.

wrong.A: The article describes only one reef.
wrong.C: The article does not describe boat repair.
wrong.D: The article focuses on one event, not a list of animal facts.

MID.prompt: Explain how Reem's training and careful choices helped lead to a scientific discovery. Use at least two details from the article.
checklist: I explained how Reem's training and choices helped.
I used at least two details from the article.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Reem's training helped her make an important discovery. Because she had practiced holding her breath and diving calmly for a long time, she was able to notice a strange pattern on the reef that did not match the coral around it. She also made a good choice when she told her uncle instead of touching the formation herself. Because they only examined it carefully, the ridge stayed safe until Dr. Huda could study it and confirm it was a rare find.

keyWords.definition: all the living things in an area, together with their environment, working together
keyWords.example: Cutting down too many trees can harm a forest ecosystem.

keyWords.definition: the hardened remains or print of a plant or animal from long ago
keyWords.example: The museum displayed a fossil of an ancient fish.

keyWords.definition: to protect something so that it stays safe or in good condition
keyWords.example: Volunteers worked to preserve the old building.

keyWords.definition: to recognize or name exactly what something is
keyWords.example: The guide helped us identify the different birds we saw.

keyWords.definition: a group of the same kind of living things growing or living closely together
keyWords.example: A colony of ants built a nest under the rock.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the article?
options: A scientist builds an artificial reef for tourists.
A curious, well-trained diver helps a marine scientist identify and protect a rare fossil within a reef ecosystem.
A diver is seriously punished by local authorities for touching a rare and ancient ocean fossil without permission.
Fossils are more common in deserts than in the sea.
questions.why: The article follows Reem's careful observation of the ridge and how it leads to Dr. Huda identifying and protecting a fossilized coral colony.

wrong.A: No one builds an artificial reef in the article.
wrong.C: Reem is praised, not punished, because she never touches the fossil.
wrong.D: The article is about a sea fossil, not a comparison with deserts.

questions.stem: What does Dr. Huda suspect the ridge actually is?
options: An old sunken ship resting quietly on the sandy ocean floor
A pile of volcanic rock
A fossil of an ancient coral colony
A type of seaweed
questions.why: The article states that Dr. Huda suspects the ridge is a fossil, the remains of an ancient coral colony.

wrong.A: There is no mention of a ship.
wrong.B: The article does not mention volcanic rock.
wrong.D: Seaweed is not mentioned in the article.

questions.stem: What does the examination team do to confirm their conclusion?
options: They compare it to known fossil records from other expeditions
They simply guess what it is based only on its unusual color alone
They ask local fishermen
They remove a piece to sell
questions.why: In the article, the team compares the pattern to known fossil records from comparable expeditions to reach their conclusion.

wrong.B: The article describes careful comparison, not a simple guess.
wrong.C: The article does not mention asking fishermen.
wrong.D: The team preserves and protects the fossil; they do not remove or sell it.

questions.stem: In the article, to identify something means to —
options: deliberately hide it from everyone else nearby
destroy it completely
ignore it
determine exactly what something is
questions.why: Dr. Huda arranges a visit specifically to identify the ridge with scientific certainty, meaning to determine exactly what it is.

wrong.A: She shares it with her team, not hides it.
wrong.B: The team wants to protect it, not destroy it.
wrong.C: The team investigates it closely; they do not ignore it.

questions.stem: Why is it important that the team confirms the ridge before disturbing it?
options: So they can sell it for money
So that they can remove it from the reef as quickly as possible
So they can be certain it deserves preservation and protection
So tourists can touch it safely
questions.why: Confirming what the formation is lets the team be sure it is worth preserving and protecting before anyone acts on it.

wrong.A: The article never mentions selling it.
wrong.B: The goal is to protect it, not remove it.
wrong.D: The article says the fossil is fragile, so touching it is discouraged.

questions.stem: Why does Dr. Huda invite Reem to join future surveys of the ecosystem?
options: Reem showed sharp observation and respect for the reef, qualities useful to a researcher
Dr. Huda needs someone to carry equipment and boxes on the boat every day of the survey
Reem's uncle paid for a spot on the team, so Dr. Huda had to say yes
It is required by law for all students to join the surveys in the area
questions.why: Dr. Huda praises Reem's sharp eyes and her careful choice not to disturb the reef, qualities she values in a future observer.

wrong.B: The article does not describe Reem as an equipment carrier.
wrong.C: The article never mentions payment.
wrong.D: There is no mention of any legal requirement.

questions.stem: How are Reem and Dr. Huda alike, based on the article?
options: Both are careful, curious people who want to understand and protect the reef
Both are afraid of the open sea and will not swim in it, not even near the shore
Both dislike free-diving and try to avoid the reef, so they stay on the boat
Both discovered the ridge at the same moment in the sea
questions.why: Both characters act with curiosity and caution, examining the ridge closely while being careful not to damage it.

wrong.B: Both dive comfortably in the open sea.
wrong.C: Reem actively trains to free-dive, and Dr. Huda dives to inspect the reef too.
wrong.D: Reem discovered it first; Dr. Huda confirmed it later.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe the step-by-step process of photographing, sending images, and later confirming the fossil, rather than skipping straight to the discovery?
options: To show that it is random luck, and not careful work, that finds fossils in the sand
To make the story longer and more exciting for the readers of the article
To show how careful observation and scientific verification lead to real discoveries
To confuse the reader about the fossil and hide how it was really found
questions.why: Walking through each careful step shows readers that real discoveries come from patience, observation, and verification, not chance.

wrong.A: The careful steps show skill and patience, not luck.
wrong.B: The steps serve a purpose; they are not filler.
wrong.D: The clear order helps readers follow the process, not confuse them.

HIGH.prompt: Do you think ordinary people, like Reem, can make a real difference in scientific discoveries? Support your argument with evidence from the article, and address at least one point someone might make against your view.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the article.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I believe ordinary people can make a real difference in scientific discoveries, and Reem's story shows why. Because she trained patiently and paid close attention while diving, she noticed a formation that turned out to be a rare fossilized coral colony, something that might otherwise have gone unnoticed. Her decision to examine it without touching it also protected the fossil until Dr. Huda's team could study it properly. Someone might argue that only trained scientists can make meaningful discoveries, but Reem's sharp observation and careful choices were just as important as Dr. Huda's scientific tests, which is why Dr. Huda invited her to help with future surveys.

LOW.stem: Who gets the photo that Uncle Faisal takes?
options: Dr. Huda
Reem's mother
The school leader
A shop worker

wrong.C: No school leader is in the article.
wrong.D: No shop worker is in the article.

Reem takes the best photo.
Reem pays for the new trip.
Reem has sharp eyes.

LOW.stem: In the article, the word rare means —
options: very big and loud
not found very often
soft like a sponge
easy to see and touch
LOW.why: Dr. Huda says the ridge is a rare find, which means it is not found often.

wrong.A: The ridge is not described as loud.
wrong.C: The text does not say the ridge is soft.
wrong.D: Reem and her uncle are told not to touch it.

LOW.stem: What happens right before Dr. Huda comes to the reef?
options: Reem goes to her school.
Uncle Faisal buys a new camera.
Uncle Faisal sends her the photo.
Reem touches the ridge once.
LOW.why: The photo is sent to Dr. Huda that night, and then she comes to the reef.

wrong.A: Going to school is not part of the article.
wrong.B: The text does not say he buys a camera.
wrong.D: Reem and her uncle do not touch the ridge.

MID.stem: What does free-diving mean in this article?
options: Diving with a big team
Diving only at night time
Swimming deep on one breath
Swimming with a tank of air
MID.why: Free-diving means swimming deep underwater on one breath, without an air tank.

wrong.A: The article does not say it needs a team.
wrong.B: Reem dives on a Friday morning.
wrong.D: Free-diving is done without a tank of air.

MID.stem: Why does Dr. Huda praise Reem?
options: For staying calm and being careful
For finding the best photo spot
For swimming deeper than the team
For buying a new camera
MID.why: The text says Dr. Huda praises Reem for her sharp eyes and for being careful not to disturb the reef.

wrong.B: Uncle Faisal takes the photos, not Reem.
wrong.C: The text does not say Reem swims deeper than the team.
wrong.D: A new camera is not mentioned.

MID.stem: Why does Uncle Faisal take photographs of the ridge?
options: To sell them to a store
To study it later without harm
To show them to other divers
To prove he is a good diver
MID.why: He takes photos so they can study the ridge more closely later without touching it.

wrong.A: Selling photos is not mentioned.
wrong.C: He sends them to a scientist, not to other divers.
wrong.D: The photos are for study, not for showing off.

MID.stem: In the article, the word formation refers to —
options: a group of swimmers
a team of scientists
a diving rule
a shape found in nature
MID.why: The ridge is called an unusual formation, which means a shape on the reef.

wrong.A: The ridge is on the reef, not a group of swimmers.
wrong.B: The scientists are called a survey team.
wrong.C: The rule about not touching is a separate idea.

HIGH.stem: What does free-diving rely on instead of a tank of compressed air?
options: A boat close to the reef
A long rope from the shore
A small underwater lamp
A single held breath
HIGH.why: The article says free-diving relies entirely on a single held breath.

wrong.A: A boat is not mentioned as a way to breathe.
wrong.B: A rope does not give air.
wrong.C: A lamp is not mentioned.

HIGH.stem: In the article, the word fragile describes the fossil as being —
options: very old and heavy
well known to divers
easy to damage
hidden beyond reach
HIGH.why: Reem is careful not to disturb the fossil because it is easy to break or harm.

wrong.A: Old does not explain why Reem is careful.
wrong.B: The fossil was not known before Reem found it.
wrong.D: Reem and the team reach it and study it.

HIGH.stem: What is one effect the discovery has on Reem?
options: She decides to stop diving.
She trains harder than ever.
She moves to another town.
She becomes afraid of the reef.
HIGH.why: After the discovery, Reem trains harder than ever, dreaming of becoming a marine scientist.

wrong.A: She keeps diving and trains harder.
wrong.C: Moving away is not mentioned.
wrong.D: She feels proud, not afraid.

HIGH.stem: Why does Uncle Faisal's rule about not touching matter more once the ridge is found to be a fossil?
options: It could harm something rare.
It would make divers tired.
It might wake the living coral.
It is a rule only for children.
HIGH.why: The team wants to preserve the rare fossil, so touching it could damage it.

wrong.B: Tiredness is not a reason given.
wrong.C: The text does not say coral can wake up.
wrong.D: The rule applies to all divers, not only children.
